subject: language_arts

unit.title: Word classes & sentence types
unit.essentialQuestion: What jobs do words do, and how do sentences come in different types?

title: The four sentence types
objectives: By the end, I can name the four sentence types and add the correct end mark.

vocabulary.definition: a telling sentence — it ends with a full stop
an asking sentence — it ends with a question mark
a bossing sentence — it starts with a bossy verb
a bursting-with-feeling sentence — it starts with What or How and ends with !

emphasize: Four types, four voices: statement tells (.), question asks (?), command bosses (bossy verb), exclamation bursts with feeling (What…/How…!).
A true exclamation SENTENCE starts with What or How — a command can use ! too, and that doesn't make it an exclamation.
Never leave a question wearing a full stop — asking needs the ? hook.

keyConcepts: command bosses → bossy verb at the front
misconceptions: ending a question with a full stop
calling anything with ! an 'exclamation sentence' (a command like Stop! uses ! too)
confusing a command with a statement (telling a fact vs telling YOU to do something)
hooks: Sentences come in four flavours, like ice cream — and each one is read in a different voice.
priorKnowledge: verbs (Lesson 16) — commands start with a bossy verb

plan.goal: Meet the four flavours through three sentences read in wildly different voices; retrieve capital + end mark.
plan.note: The voices ARE the hook — bossy, questioning-up, tired-flat. Get the child using their asking voice immediately.
plan.successCriteria: Child answers 'a capital letter and an end mark' and copies the rising asking voice.

script.say: Sentences come in four flavours, like ice cream! There's TELLING sentences, ASKING sentences, BOSSING sentences, and BURSTING-with-feeling sentences. Each one has its own special ending. Listen: STOP! — bossy. Where are you? — hear my voice go up? I am tired. — flat as a pancake. Now you try the asking one — and first, quick check: what two things does every sentence start and end with?
script.adaptHints: Ham up the three voices. If the retrieval is shaky: 'a sentence opens with a capital and closes with a mark — today we learn WHICH mark.'

blocks.prompt: Say 'Where are you?' in your best ASKING voice — make it go UP at the end!

stuckProtocol: If the rising voice doesn't come: say it together twice, exaggerating the lift on 'you?', then let the child solo it.

plan.goal: Name all four types with their end marks; model sorting Stop! / Where are you? / I am tired.
plan.note: The table is the anchor for the whole unit. Land the two traps early: questions never wear a full stop; What/How starts a true exclamation.
plan.successCriteria: Child can point to the right row for 'tells', 'asks', 'bosses' and 'bursts'.

script.say: Four types. A STATEMENT just tells you something and ends in a full stop: Dogs bark. A QUESTION asks something and needs a question mark: Why do dogs bark? A COMMAND bosses you about with a bossy verb at the front: Tidy up. Sit down. An EXCLAMATION bursts with feeling and properly starts with What or How, ending in an exclamation mark: What a mess! How fast it runs! Watch me sort: Stop! — bossy verb, that's a command. Where are you? — asks, question. I am tired. — tells, statement.
script.adaptHints: Read each example in its voice every single time. Point at the table row as each type is named.

plan.goal: Shared sort: does each sentence tell, ask, boss or burst? Child drags four cards under the type labels.
plan.note: Ask 'tell, ask, boss or burst?' before every card — that four-word question is the tool.
plan.successCriteria: Child sorts all four cards correctly, reading each in its matching voice.

script.say: Sort with me — for each one, ask yourself: does it tell, ask, boss or burst? Dogs bark. — telling? asking? … it tells, so statement, full stop! Now Why do dogs bark? — hear the voice go up? Your turn with the rest — read each one aloud in its voice, then drag it home.
script.adaptHints: If the child hesitates, read the sentence in an exaggerated voice and let the voice give the answer away.

blocks.prompt: Tell, ask, boss or burst? Sort each sentence into its type.

check.question: Which type is 'What a mess!' — and how do you know?
check.expectedAnswer: An exclamation — it bursts with feeling, starts with 'What' and ends with !

wrongAnswers.why: saw the ! and assumed bossing
wrongAnswers.remedy: Is it telling you to DO something? No bossy verb at the front — it starts with 'What' and bursts with feeling. Which type starts with What or How?

wrongAnswers.why: treated it as plain telling
wrongAnswers.remedy: Read it in a flat voice… it doesn't fit! It BURSTS. Which type bursts with feeling?

plan.goal: Key diagnostic: 'Close the window.' — a command, spotted by its bossy verb, NOT by any mark.
plan.note: 'Statement' means telling/bossing confusion; 'exclamation' means mark/type confusion. Probe the first word's job after a correct answer.
plan.successCriteria: Child answers 'command' and explains the first word is bossing you to do something.

script.say: Type detective! What type is this: Close the window. Think — does it tell, ask, boss or burst? And be ready to tell me how you know.
script.adaptHints: After a correct answer, probe: 'How do you know — what's the first word doing?' (bossing you to do something).

blocks.prompt: What type is: Close the window.
blocks.explain: It starts with the bossy verb 'close' — it's telling YOU to do something. That's a command.

check.question: What type is 'Close the window.'?
check.expectedAnswer: A command — it starts with a bossy verb (close)

wrongAnswers.why: confused telling with bossing
wrongAnswers.remedy: Is it telling you a fact, or telling YOU to do something? It's bossing you — close! — so which type is it?

wrongAnswers.why: confused mark with type — it 'feels strong'
wrongAnswers.remedy: Does it start with What or How? No. A true exclamation does. This one bosses — so it's a…?

plan.goal: Independent sorting and marking: eight sentences into four types, correct end mark on each.
plan.note: Director draws from practiceBank, start level 2. Watch for: full stop on a question; any-!-is-an-exclamation; missing the bossy-verb cue.
plan.successCriteria: Child sorts at least six of eight sentences correctly with the right end marks, including a command with !.

script.say: Your ice-cream counter now! Sentences are coming — sort each one into its flavour and give it the right ending. Say each one aloud in its voice — the voice tells you the type.
script.adaptHints: Build sentences around the child's interests (their pet, football, space). The four-flavour question never changes: tell, ask, boss or burst?

stuckProtocol: Name why: 'Let's ask: does it tell, ask, boss or burst?'
Step down: put the four type-cards back on screen as anchors and read the sentence aloud in each voice — which fits?
ONE hint: 'Read it — does your voice go UP? Then it's a question.'
Re-ask a smaller version: one card only.
Keep it safe: 'Four flavours take practice — let's taste this one again.'

plan.goal: Child names all four types and their marks; end on a win.
plan.note: Child-led. Sneak the command-with-! subtlety into the praise.
plan.successCriteria: Child recites: statement (.), question (?), command (bossy verb, . or !), exclamation (What/How…!).

script.say: Name the four sentence types and the mark each one ends with. … Brilliant. You read each one in the right voice and matched its mark — even spotting that a strong-feeling sentence isn't always an exclamation type. Sharp work.
script.adaptHints: If the child forgets one, hum its voice (bossy / rising / flat / bursting) as the clue rather than naming it.

block.prompt: Dogs bark. — does it tell, ask, boss or burst?
block.explain: It just tells you a fact, in a flat voice, ending with a full stop. Statement.

wrongAnswers.why: muddled telling a fact with telling YOU to act
wrongAnswers.remedy: Is it ordering you to do something? No bossy verb at the front — it just tells. Which type tells?

wrongAnswers.why: any dog excitement feels like bursting
wrongAnswers.remedy: Read it flat: Dogs bark. Does it start with What or How? It's calm telling — which type?

hints: Read it aloud — is your voice flat, up, bossy or bursting?

reteach.say: The four-word tool works every time: tell, ask, boss or burst? Dogs bark — it just TELLS me a fact, flat voice, full stop. Telling sentences are statements.

block.definition: a telling sentence — flat voice, full stop: Dogs bark.

wrongAnswers.why: full stop on a question — the classic trap
wrongAnswers.remedy: Read it aloud — does your voice go UP at the end? Asking sentences need the special hook. Which mark is the hook?

wrongAnswers.why: reached for the most exciting mark
wrongAnswers.remedy: Is it bursting with feeling, or ASKING something? Your voice goes up — which mark catches an asking voice?

hints: Say it aloud — voice up at the end?
Asking sentences end with the little hook: ?

reteach.say: Here's the rule that never bends: if the sentence ASKS, it wears the question-mark hook. Where are you? — voice up, hook on. A full stop on a question is like a hat on backwards!

practiceBank.skill: sort sentences into the four types

block.prompt: Sort the sentences: tell, ask, boss or burst?

practiceBank.expectedAnswer: I am tired. → Statement · Where are you? → Question · Sit down. → Command · How fast it runs! → Exclamation

wrongAnswers.why: telling/bossing confusion
wrongAnswers.remedy: Is it telling a fact, or telling YOU to do something? Sit! — that's bossing. Which bucket bosses?

wrongAnswers.why: 'how' looks like a question word
wrongAnswers.remedy: Sneaky! Read it aloud — is it ASKING how fast, or BURSTING about how fast? It starts How and ends ! — a true exclamation.

hints: Read each one in a voice — the voice gives it away.
Bossy verb at the front → command.

reteach.say: One at a time, with the tool. I am tired — tells, statement. Where are you — voice up, asks, question. Sit down — bossy verb first, command. How fast it runs — starts with How, bursts with feeling — exclamation. Tell, ask, boss or burst: every sentence answers one.

practiceBank.skill: identify a command by its bossy verb

block.prompt: What type is: Shut the door.
block.explain: The bossy verb 'shut' is at the front, telling YOU to do something — a command.

wrongAnswers.why: confused telling with bossing
wrongAnswers.remedy: Who has to DO something here? YOU do — shut! A telling sentence doesn't order anyone about. Which type does?

wrongAnswers.why: strong feeling ≠ exclamation type
wrongAnswers.remedy: Does it start with What or How? No — it starts with a bossy verb. Which type starts bossy?

hints: Look at the very first word — what's it doing?
A verb at the front, bossing you → command.

reteach.say: Commands give themselves away at the very first word: a bossy verb. Shut the door. Sit down. Stop. The verb marches out front and tells YOU what to do — that's a command, whatever mark it ends with.

block.definition: starts with a bossy verb — Shut… Sit… Stop… — telling you to do something

practiceBank.skill: read each type in the right voice

block.prompt: Read this in your best BOSSY voice, then tell me its type: Tidy your room.

practiceBank.expectedAnswer: Reads it in a firm bossy voice and names it a command

wrongAnswers.answer: reads it as a question (voice up)
wrongAnswers.why: asking voice attached to a bossing sentence
wrongAnswers.remedy: Tidy your room? — sounds like a choice! It's not asking, it's TELLING you. Try it firm and flat: Tidy your room.

wrongAnswers.why: telling/bossing confusion
wrongAnswers.remedy: Is it sharing a fact, or ordering YOU about? The bossy verb 'tidy' is at the front — which type is that?

hints: Commands sound firm, like a captain.
First word 'tidy' — what's it doing to you?

reteach.say: Each type has a voice costume. Statements: flat. Questions: up at the end. Commands: firm, like a captain — Tidy your room! Exclamations: bursting. Say the sentence in each voice and only ONE will fit.

block.caption: flat · rising · firm · bursting — four voices, four types

wrongAnswers.why: 'what' at the front looked like a question
wrongAnswers.remedy: Read it — is it ASKING what the mess is? No, it's BURSTING about the mess! What/How + feeling ends with which mark?

wrongAnswers.why: flat mark on a bursting sentence
wrongAnswers.remedy: Say it flat: what a mess. All the feeling drained away! An exclamation bursts — which mark bursts with it?

hints: It starts with 'What' and bursts with feeling.
Exclamations end with the excited mark.

reteach.say: What a mess! starts with What and BURSTS with feeling — that's a true exclamation sentence, and it always ends with the exclamation mark. What or How in front, ! at the back.

block.definition: starts with What or How, bursts with feeling, ends with ! — What a mess!

practiceBank.skill: distinguish exclamation TYPE from ! the mark

block.prompt: Stretch! 'Stop!' ends with an exclamation mark. Is it an exclamation SENTENCE?
options: Yes — anything with ! is an exclamation
No — it's a command; a true exclamation starts with What or How
block.explain: The ! shows strong feeling, but the TYPE comes from the sentence's job: 'Stop!' bosses with a bossy verb — a command. True exclamation sentences start with What or How.

practiceBank.expectedAnswer: No — it's a command; a true exclamation starts with What or How

wrongAnswers.answer: Yes — anything with ! is an exclamation
wrongAnswers.why: mark/type confusion — the unit's subtlest trap
wrongAnswers.remedy: The mark shows feeling, but the TYPE comes from the job. What is 'Stop!' doing — bursting, or bossing you? And what do true exclamations start with?

wrongAnswers.why: loudness mistaken for type
wrongAnswers.remedy: Loud isn't a type! Check the first word: 'stop' is a bossy verb. Which type starts with a bossy verb?

hints: The mark and the type are different things.
True exclamation sentences start with What or How.

reteach.say: Here's the expert-level secret: the exclamation MARK is just a feeling-flag — commands may borrow it. Stop! is still a command, because a bossy verb leads it. A true exclamation SENTENCE begins What or How: What a mess! How fast it runs! First word first, mark second.

practiceBank.skill: sort trickier sentences including a command with !

block.prompt: Master sort — careful, one command is wearing an exclamation mark!

practiceBank.expectedAnswer: How fast it runs! → Exclamation · Run to the gate! → Command · The gate is open. → Statement · Is the gate open? → Question

wrongAnswers.why: sorted by the mark instead of the job
wrongAnswers.remedy: It ends with !, but check the first word: 'run' — a bossy verb ordering you about. Marks can lie; first words don't.

wrongAnswers.why: 'how' read as a question word
wrongAnswers.remedy: Is it asking you HOW fast, or bursting ABOUT how fast? No answer is wanted — it's a burst. Which bucket?

hints: Sort by the JOB, not the mark.
Check the first word of each sentence.

reteach.say: Two sentences end with ! — but only one is an exclamation. Run to the gate! starts with a bossy verb: command in party clothes. How fast it runs! starts with How: true exclamation. Job first, mark second — that's how experts sort.

practiceBank.skill: write one sentence of each type

block.prompt: Grand finale! Write one statement, one question, one command and one exclamation about a cat — with the right end mark on each.
block.sample: The cat is asleep. Why is the cat asleep? Wake the cat. What a lazy cat!

practiceBank.expectedAnswer: Four sentences, one of each type, with correct end marks (exclamation starting What/How)

wrongAnswers.answer: question written with a full stop
wrongAnswers.why: the classic question-mark slip
wrongAnswers.remedy: Read your asking sentence aloud — voice up? Then it needs the hook. Swap the mark.

wrongAnswers.why: statement with a ! — not the Year 2 exclamation form
wrongAnswers.remedy: Strong feeling, yes — but a true exclamation starts with What or How. Try starting yours with 'What a…'.

hints: One at a time: tell it, ask it, boss it, burst it.
For the exclamation, start with 'What a…' or 'How…'.

reteach.say: Take ONE idea and wear all four hats. Tell it: The cat is asleep. Ask it: Why is the cat asleep? Boss it: Wake the cat. Burst it: What a lazy cat! Same cat, four flavours, four marks.

block.title: One cat, four types
steps: Ask: Why is the cat asleep?

adaptivity.levelUp: 2 consecutive correct at the current level → next level; at level 3, interleave sorting, end-mark and mark-vs-type items.
adaptivity.levelDown: 2 misses on the same skill → run the item's reteach with the four type-anchors on screen, then a level-1 item (single sentence, tell/ask only).
adaptivity.masterySignal: 3+ correct across levels 2–3 including one command identified by its bossy verb and one command-with-! NOT called an exclamation → mastery ≥ 0.8 for 'four sentence types'.
struggleProtocol: Name why: 'Let's ask: does it tell, ask, boss or burst?'
Step down: four type-cards as anchors; read the sentence aloud in each voice.
ONE hint: 'Read it — does your voice go UP? Then it's a question.'
Re-ask a smaller version (one card), build back.
Keep it safe: 'Four flavours take practice — let's taste this one again.'
adaptivity.personalization: Build the practice sentences around the learner's interests (their pet, football, dinosaurs). The tell/ask/boss/burst tool and the voices never change.
adaptivity.endOnSuccess: Finish on a winnable sort or end-mark item; praise the process — 'you checked the first word's job instead of trusting the mark.'

differentiation.support: Four type-cards stay on screen as anchors; the character reads each sentence aloud in its voice before the child sorts.
differentiation.stretch: Write one sentence of each of the four types with correct end marks; explain why Stop! is a command, not an exclamation.

extension: Take one idea (the cat) and turn it into all four types, reading each in its voice — flat, rising, firm, bursting.
assessmentEvidence: Child sorts at least six of eight sentences into the correct type with the right end mark, including identifying a command by its bossy verb.
revisitLater: Lesson 19 zooms in on questions and exclamations (the special marks). Re-pose 'what type is…?' as retrieval next session.
